subject: Hosted API MFN & CPI-cap anchoring — BlueWave committed tier
messages:
From: Carlos Ruiz <carlos.ruiz@bluewave.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@bluewave.com
Date: Mon, 19 Jul 2027 15:03:00 -0400
Subject: Hosted API pricing — MFN / CPI cap request

Hi Jonas / Vanessa,

Thanks for the demo last week — the team is excited to move forward. As we begin internal procurement, two items came up that we need Redwood to confirm before we can clear a committed-volume agreement for our production rollout:

1) MFN (most-favored-nation) treatment for hosted API pricing for our committed tier. We need assurance we aren’t paying more than comparable customers for the same hosted API product.
2) CPI-based cap on price increases — our procurement policy requires limiting annual price increases tied to CPI to a defined cap (we’d prefer 2%).

We’re planning a 12–24 month commit for ~1.2B tokens/mo at launch (growth expected). Attached is the updated RFP (BlueWave_RFP_v3.pdf) with the commit outline.

Can you confirm Redwood's position on MFN scope and whether you can accommodate a CPI cap (and for how many months)? If you can’t do full MFN, please propose a practical carve-out list and any alternative credit/guardrail structure.

Appreciate a one-page summary we can attach to our procurement packet — a quick yes/no plus exceptions will do.

Best,
Carlos Ruiz
Head of Platform Partnerships
BlueWave Analytics

--
Attachment: BlueWave_RFP_v3.pdf (PDF, 1.2MB stub)

From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
To: Carlos Ruiz <carlos.ruiz@bluewave.com>
Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 20 Jul 2027 09:12:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Hosted API pricing — MFN / CPI cap request

Hi Carlos — thanks for the clear ask and the RFP. Quick read — congrats on the scale.

High level answer up front: we can structure a pragmatic agreement that balances MFN-like protections, a CPI cap, and commercial flexibility. Below is a draft of the tradeoffs and a proposed term-band we think procurement will accept. Laura (who owns pricing/product bundles) is looped for product/operational constraints.

Proposal (summary):
- Commit tier: 1.2B tokens/mo baseline for 12 months with an optional 6-month extension tied to growth milestones.
- Price-lock: 12 months firm on per-token list price for the committed tier. After 12 months, price adjustments limited to an agreed CPI cap (proposed 2.5% annually) unless mutually agreed otherwise.
- MFN: Redwood will provide MFN for materially similar hosted API offerings to customers in the same commitment tier and region. MFN carve-outs: public promotions (limited-duration offers), channel partner discounts, and strategic partner reseller pricing.
- Credits: If a price reduction is later published that would have applied retroactively, Redwood will issue a one-time credit to BlueWave for the delta for the remainder of the then-current billing period (not retroactive beyond that).

Operational/notes:
- We need to lock model families and quantization/variant SKU definitions into the term sheet so MFN comparisons are apples-to-apples.
- For CPI cap enforcement we’ll need an agreed CPI index (US CPI-U) and a 30-day lookback calculation window.

Next steps: Vanessa / Laura — can you draft a short term-sheet that captures the above and includes a clause limiting MFN scope to "published list prices for equivalent commitment tiers and deployment modes"? Carlos — if that sounds directionally acceptable I’ll circulate a draft term sheet by EOD tomorrow.

Cheers,
Jonas Weber
Senior Account Executive
Redwood Inference

From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>

Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 20 Jul 2027 13:45:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Hosted API pricing — MFN / CPI cap request

Hi Carlos — quick note from commercial side. Appreciate the specificity. A few additional clarifications to help procurement: 

- MFN scope: we can agree MFN for "equivalent hosted API product and committed-volume tier" but need to exclude: (a) promotional/public flash pricing, (b) pre-signed channel/reseller agreements, and (c) bespoke enterprise on-prem bundles. This keeps our marketplace and partner programs viable.
- CPI cap: we can accept a 2.5% annual CPI cap for price increases applied post the initial 12-month lock. For a 2% cap we’d need to either shorten the price-lock window or require a higher commit/term (24 months).
- 24-month lock: as an alternative, if BlueWave wants a 24-month firm price-lock we can offer that at a reduced per-token baseline (we’d need a committed 24-month minimum and an escalation clause for usage >2x baseline).

I’ll attach a short draft term-sheet outlining three options (12m lock + 2.5% CPI cap; 18m lock + 2.25% cap; 24m lock + 2% cap + higher commit) so procurement can pick the preferred structure.

Attaching Redwood_Draft_Term_Sheet_v2.docx (high level).

If helpful, we can set a short call tomorrow to walk procurement through the MFN carve-outs.

Thanks,
Vanessa Ortiz
Head of Sales — Enterprise
Redwood Inference

--

From: Carlos Ruiz <carlos.ruiz@bluewave.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@bluewave.com
Date: Wed, 21 Jul 2027 10:02:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Hosted API pricing — MFN / CPI cap request

Thanks Vanessa/Jonas — appreciate the options. A few counterpoints from procurement: 

- MFN: BlueWave’s legal team requires MFN that covers any published list pricing or any published tiered offers for hosted API in the US region. We can accept carve-outs for narrow channel reseller programs, but public marketplace discounts (e.g., launch promos) must be captured by MFN if they are available to the general market.
- CPI cap: procurement cannot accept >2% for our budget planning. If Redwood cannot accept 2% then we will need to negotiate a credit mechanism to cover the delta.
- Price-lock duration: 24 months is preferred; 18 months is acceptable if the CPI cap is reduced to 2%.

We’re aiming to finalize commercial terms by end of next week. Would you be able to indicate which of the three options in your term-sheet maps to a best-and-final commercial offer if BlueWave signs a 24-month commit? Also please summarize exactly what is considered an MFN-comparable offering.

—Carlos

From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
To: Carlos Ruiz <carlos.ruiz@bluewave.com>
Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 22 Jul 2027 11:18:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Hosted API pricing — MFN / CPI cap request

Carlos — thanks for the clear feedback. After internal alignment with product and legal, here’s a concise "best-and-final" we can put on the table for a 24-month committed agreement (we can follow-up with formal term-sheet/Docusign if this is acceptable):

Best-and-final for 24-month commit (summary):
- Commit: 24 months, 1.2B tokens/mo baseline.
- Price-lock: firm 18 months on per-token list price for the committed tier, then CPI adjustments up to a 2.5% cap annually for the remainder of the term.
- CPI approach: US CPI-U as published by BLS, annual adjustment applied on the anniversary using the 12-month rolling average; cap = 2.5% (we can consider a 2.0% cap only with additional commercial credit or a higher commit level).
- MFN scope: MFN applies to Redwood public list prices and published tiered discounts for the same hosted API service in the US region, for customers with equivalent committed-volume tiers. Carve-outs: limited-duration public promos shorter than 30 days (unless extended); partner volume rebates; pre-negotiated reseller programs.
- Remedy: If a qualifying lower public list price is published during the term, Redwood will provide a one-time credit equal to the price difference applied pro rata for the remainder of the then-current billing period. We cannot make retroactive adjustments beyond the current billing period.

To address your procurement team's 2% requirement: we can accept a 2.0% CPI cap if BlueWave increases committed baseline to 1.5B tokens/mo OR agrees to a one-time upfront commitment credit that compensates the expected delta between 2% and 2.5% across year two (we can model this in the term sheet).

If this directionally works I’ll circulate a formal term-sheet (clean + redline) and route it to legal for a DocuSign. Proposed next step: 30-minute connect tomorrow to run through MFN comparability language and the CPI calculation. Please pick a slot and I’ll send calendar invite.

Thanks,
Jonas Weber
Senior Account Executive
Redwood Inference
